text:
anh: Heads-up — after flipping the FA v3 default kernel in canary today we saw a 10-15% increase in p95 on the 16k token long-seq workload. Noticed on a 4-GPU node pool only, not on multi-node batches.

taylan: ugh. which metric exactly? p50 also shifted?

anh: p50 ~1% up, p95 ~12% up, p99 ~3% (weird). CPU steal/IO looks normal. GPU utilization slightly lower.

cassandra: do we have the kernel selection trace? might be falling back to the per-slice slow path for certain seq len shapes.

anh: pasted snippet from traces: `kernel=flashattn_v3, seq_len=1024, batch=4, workspace_alloc=chunked, path=main` — then `pad_frag=true` entries right before OOM-retry.

pri: pad fragmentation + allocator interaction is a known issue with bf16 alloc on OOM-retry. v3 uses larger temporary workspace peaks for some workspace shapes. If batch coalescing changed, that could increase tail.

anh: we didn't change batching on canary. Kernel selector toggle alone caused it. Selector now prefers v3 for shapes with seqlen>512.

taylan: can you dump the allocator histogram and workspace fragment counts? also which cuDNN/cuobj versions on that pool? v3 may be nudging different kernel codepaths that expose allocator fragmentation.

anh: attached two lines from node logs: `allocator_free_frag_ratio=0.32, max_workspace=1.8GB, avg_workspace=1.2GB` and `kernel_exec_ms: main=28.1, fallback=31.7, retry=45.9` — fallback slower as expected but main also regressed vs baseline.

cassandra: main regression suggests launch configuration changed (grid/block) or internal memcpy pattern. Did the v3 build include the new tiled transpose micro-optimizations? Those can increase L2 pressure on some SMs.

pri: also check kv-cache reuse. If v3's kernel warms different shared memory regions it could affect cached KV prefetch timing and cause small extra latency for subsequent tokens.

anh: good call. I can add tracepoints for KV hit latency. Plan: 1) enable detailed kernel telemetry for 1h on canary; 2) run synthetic repro with batch sizes [1,2,4,8] and seq lenses [256,512,1024,2048]; 3) revert selector to prefer v2 for >1024 and compare.

taylan: add a perf counter for L2 read/write and shared mem occupation if possible. Also pin one canary node to the older cuda/cuobj release to rule out driver interactions.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: started canary rollout to pool "fa-v3-probe" (5 nodes).

cassandra: FYI, when you run synthetic, include the small-batch long-seq mix that matches traffic (lots of batch=1 with seqlen bursts). We saw similar in q4.

anh: ack. I'll capture p50/p95/p99 and raw kernel duration histograms and post a short summary. If we confirm allocator fragmentation, next step is to try alternative workspace pooling (pre-reserve) or fall back to v2 for fragmentation-heavy shapes.

pri: one more thought — quantized paths: are we running bf16 vs fp16 differences? v3 had a micro-optim that behaves differently on bf16 rounding which changed instruction mix. Might be cheaper overall but worse on tails.

anh: noted. I'll include bf16/fp16 runs. should have initial numbers in ~2h.

taylan: sweet. if you need help crafting the synthetic harness, ping me.

anh: thanks — will update here with numbers + raw traces. :pray:
